1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 Christian Merten. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: Christian Merten
5	-/
6	import Mathlib
7	
8	/-!
9	# The Jacobian challenge — statement file (with field base change)
10	
11	This is the single, self-contained **statement file** of the project: it collects every
12	definition, instance, and theorem needed to *state* the main result, and nothing else. A reviewer
13	reads this one file, compares it against the original challenge (`references/challenge.lean`, by
14	Christian Merten) and its base-change extension, and is convinced the project formalizes the right
15	thing. The genuinely-missing pieces are `sorry`; the base-change scaffolding (`baseChange`, the
16	stability instances, `idIso`, `compIso`, and `Jacobian.congr` derived from `Jacobian.functor`) is
17	genuinely proved here. Proofs of the `sorry`s live in the rest of the `AlgebraicJacobian/` tree and
18	must not weaken or restate any signature below.
19	
20	By a **smooth curve** we mean a geometrically irreducible, smooth scheme of relative dimension one
21	over a field, proper over that field.
22	
23	## Main definitions
24	
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` — genus of a proper, smooth curve.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` — the Jacobian of a proper, smooth curve.
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map associated to a `k`-rational point.
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.functor` — functoriality of the Jacobian, bundled as a single
29	  contravariant functor `(Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec k))`.
30	
31	## Main theorems
32	
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` — the Jacobian is smooth of relative
34	  dimension `g = genus C`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` — the universal property: the Jacobian is
36	  the Albanese variety of `C`.
37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.baseChangeIso` — the Jacobian commutes with base change of fields,
38	  together with the identity/cocycle coherences (`baseChangeIso_id`, `baseChangeIso_comp`) and the
39	  Abel–Jacobi compatibility `baseChange_ofCurve`.
40	
41	## Notes
42	
43	`noncomputable` is on the data-carrying declarations: their honest realizations rest on
44	noncomputable Mathlib constructions. Names, argument types, and argument order are verbatim from
45	the challenge; the `noncomputable` modifier is not a signature change.
46	-/
47	
48	set_option autoImplicit false
49	
50	universe u
51	
52	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory MonObj
53	
54	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
55	
56	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
57	  -- smooth curve
58	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
59	  -- proper
60	  [IsProper C.hom]
61	  -- geometrically irreducible
62	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
63	
64	/-- The category of smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curves over `k`, with morphisms the
65	morphisms of `k`-schemes. -/
66	structure Curve (k : Type u) [Field k] where
67	  /-- The underlying `k`-scheme. -/
68	  carrier : Over (Spec (.of k))
69	  [isProper : IsProper carrier.hom]
70	  [smoothOfRelativeDimension : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 carrier.hom]
71	  [geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible carrier.hom]
72	
73	attribute [instance] Curve.isProper Curve.smoothOfRelativeDimension Curve.geometricallyIrreducible
74	
75	noncomputable instance (k : Type u) [Field k] : Category (Curve k) where
76	  Hom X Y := X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier
77	  id X := 𝟙 X.carrier
78	  comp f g := f ≫ g
79	  id_comp := Category.id_comp
80	  comp_id := Category.comp_id
81	  assoc := Category.assoc
82	
83	-- data
84	/-- The genus of a smooth proper curve. -/
85	noncomputable def genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
86	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=
87	  sorry
88	
89	-- data
90	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`. -/
91	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
92	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
93	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
94	  sorry
95	
96	namespace Jacobian
97	
98	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
99	
100	-- data
101	/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
102	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) :=
103	  sorry
104	
105	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is smooth of relative dimension `g` over `k`, where `g` is the
106	genus of `C`. -/
107	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
108	  sorry
109	
110	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is proper over `k`. -/
111	instance : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom :=
112	  sorry
113	
114	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
115	instance : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
116	  sorry
117	
118	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian associated
119	to a `k`-rational point of `C`. -/
120	noncomputable def ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : C ⟶ Jacobian C :=
121	  sorry
122	
123	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map sends the `k`-rational point `P` to `0`, where `0` (denoted by `η`) is the
124	neutral element of the group scheme `Jacobian C`. -/
125	theorem comp_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
126	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
127	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
128	    P ≫ ofCurve P = η[Jacobian C] :=
129	  sorry
130	
131	/--
132	The universal property of the Jacobian variety: For any abelian variety `A`, any morphism
133	`f : C ⟶ A` with `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the Jacobian of `C`. In other words,
134	`Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.
135	-/
136	theorem exists_unique_ofCurve_comp (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
137	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
138	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
139	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [Smooth A.hom] [IsProper A.hom] [GrpObj A]
140	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
141	    ∃! (g : Jacobian C ⟶ A), f = ofCurve P ≫ g :=
142	  sorry
143	
144	/-- **Functoriality of the Jacobian**, bundled as a single contravariant functor: a curve goes to
145	its Jacobian group scheme over `k`, and a morphism of curves to the pullback of line bundles. The
146	functor laws (`map_id`, `map_comp`) are embedded in this `Functor`. The object action is pinned to
147	the `Jacobian` above, so everything downstream stays phrased in terms of `Jacobian C`. -/
148	noncomputable def functor (k : Type u) [Field k] :
149	    (Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))) where
150	  obj X := .mk (Jacobian X.unop.carrier)
151	  map _ := sorry
152	  map_id := sorry
153	  map_comp := sorry
154	
155	end Jacobian
156	
157	/-! ## Base change of fields
158	
159	Base change of `k`-schemes along `k → L` sends `X` to `X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. These definitions and
160	the stability instances are genuine (no `sorry`); they set up the statements of the base-change
161	compatibility of the Jacobian. -/
162	
163	/-- Base change of `k`-schemes along a field homomorphism `k → L`, i.e. `X ↦ X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`.
164	-/
165	noncomputable abbrev baseChange (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
166	    Over (Spec (.of k)) ⥤ Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
167	  Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
168	
169	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
170	    [IsProper C.hom] : IsProper ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
171	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
172	
173	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
174	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
175	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
176	
177	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
178	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
179	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
180	  have : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1) :=
181	    smoothOfRelativeDimension_isStableUnderBaseChange 1
182	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
183	
184	-- The coherences mention curves of the form `(𝟭 _).obj C` and `(F ⋙ G).obj C`.
185	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom] :
186	    IsProper ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
187	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
188	    GeometricallyIrreducible ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
189	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
190	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
191	
192	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
193	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom] :
194	    IsProper ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
195	  inferInstanceAs (IsProper ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
196	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
197	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
198	    GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
199	  inferInstanceAs (GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
200	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
201	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
202	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
203	  inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
204	
205	/-- Base change along `k → k` is the identity functor. -/
206	noncomputable def baseChange.idIso (k : Type u) [Field k] :
207	    baseChange k k ≅ 𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k))) :=
208	  eqToIso (by
209	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k))) = Over.pullback (𝟙 _)
210	    rw [Algebra.algebraMap_self, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]) ≪≫ Over.pullbackId
211	
212	/-- Base change along a tower `k → L → M` is the composite of the two base changes. -/
213	noncomputable def baseChange.compIso (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
214	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M] :
215	    baseChange k M ≅ baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M :=
216	  eqToIso (by
217	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M))) =
218	      Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L M)) ≫
219	        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
220	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq]) ≪≫
221	    Over.pullbackComp _ _
222	
223	namespace Jacobian
224	
225	/-- The Jacobian respects isomorphisms of curves — *derived* from the bundled functor
226	`Jacobian.functor` via `Functor.mapIso`, not a primitive. Used to compare the two sides of the
227	cocycle, whose curves agree only up to `baseChange.compIso`. -/
228	noncomputable def congr {k : Type u} [Field k] {C C' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
229	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
230	    [IsProper C'.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C'.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C'.hom]
231	    (e : C ≅ C') :
232	    (.mk (Jacobian C) : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) ≅ .mk (Jacobian C') :=
233	  let j : (⟨C⟩ : Curve k) ≅ ⟨C'⟩ :=
234	    { hom := e.hom, inv := e.inv, hom_inv_id := e.hom_inv_id, inv_hom_id := e.inv_hom_id }
235	  (Jacobian.functor k).mapIso j.symm.op
236	
237	/-- **The base-change condition.** Jacobians commute with base change of fields: a canonical
238	isomorphism `Jac(C)_L ≅ Jac(C_L)`, as group schemes over `L`. -/
239	noncomputable def baseChangeIso (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
240	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
241	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
242	    (baseChange k L).mapGrp.obj (.mk (Jacobian C)) ≅ .mk (Jacobian ((baseChange k L).obj C)) :=
243	  sorry
244	
245	/-! ## Functoriality: the base change isomorphisms form a coherent system. -/
246	
247	/-- Identity coherence. -/
248	theorem baseChangeIso_id (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
249	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
250	    baseChangeIso k k C =
251	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.idIso k)).app _
252	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpIdIso (C := Over (Spec (.of k)))).app _
253	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).symm :=
254	  sorry
255	
256	/-- Cocycle coherence for a tower `k → L → M`. -/
257	theorem baseChangeIso_comp (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
258	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M]
259	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
260	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
261	    baseChangeIso k M C
262	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.compIso k L M).app C) =
263	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.compIso k L M)).app _
264	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpCompIso (F := baseChange k L) (G := baseChange L M)).app _
265	        ≪≫ (baseChange L M).mapGrp.mapIso (baseChangeIso k L C)
266	        ≪≫ baseChangeIso L M ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
267	  sorry
268	
269	/-! ## Compatibility with the Abel-Jacobi map -/
270	
271	variable {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
272	
273	theorem baseChange_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
274	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
275	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
276	    (baseChange k L).map (ofCurve P) ≫ (baseChangeIso k L C).hom.hom.hom =
277	      ofCurve (Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε (baseChange k L) ≫ (baseChange k L).map P) :=
278	  sorry
279	
280	end Jacobian
281	
282	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	# AlgebraicJacobian (rebuild)
2	
3	<!-- archon:readme -->
4	
5	## Project
6	
7	A **from-scratch rebuild** of the Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the **Jacobian of a smooth,
8	proper, geometrically irreducible curve** over a field (Christian Merten's AI challenge, inspired by
9	Kevin Buzzard's Riemann-surface version). By a smooth curve we mean a geometrically irreducible,
10	smooth scheme of relative dimension one over a field.
11	
12	This project supplies the missing definitions (`genus`, `Jacobian`, the Abel–Jacobi map `ofCurve`)
13	and theorems (the Jacobian is smooth of relative dimension equal to the genus, proper, geometrically
14	irreducible, and is the Albanese variety of the curve, characterized by the universal property
15	`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`). It targets the **extended** challenge: additionally, the Jacobian is
16	**functorial** in the curve (`Jacobian.functor`) and **commutes with base change of fields**
17	(`baseChangeIso` with identity and cocycle coherences, and Abel–Jacobi compatibility
18	`baseChange_ofCurve`), which makes the construction canonical.
19	
20	It is rebuilt rather than continued: the goal is a cleaner, more general, mathlib-idiomatic
21	infrastructure and a shorter, clearer path to the conclusion. The existing project
22	`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` may be **read** when genuinely blocked, but nothing is
23	copied from it — every declaration is rewritten. The rebuild is driven by its Archon Horizon task,
24	which carries the full charter (target, constraints, working model, and phases).
25	
26	## Structure
27	
28	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` — the single, reviewable **statement file**: every signature a
29	  reviewer must trust, and nothing else. Agents own the proofs, never these signatures.
30	- `AlgebraicJacobian/` — the infrastructure that discharges the statement (added as the rebuild
31	  proceeds; no file exceeds 500 lines; layout mirrors the mathematical structure of the paper).
32	- `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — the library root import list.
33	- `blueprint/` — a clean **mathematical** blueprint (no Lean code in the prose; nodes carry `\lean{}`
34	  and `\source{}` anchors). Build with `leanblueprint pdf` / `leanblueprint web`.
35	- `archon-protected.yaml` — the mathematician-owned signatures agents must not modify.
36	
37	## Sources
38	
39	The shared workspace-root [`references/`](../../references/) library (indexed by
40	`references/manifest.yaml`) backs the blueprint. Read a source before citing it with `\source{...}`.
41	
42	## How to build
43	
44	```bash
45	lake build           # compile (olean cache shared via ../../.lake-packages)
46	```

text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/Axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/task-status

A task is the unit of work a run dispatches. **You own its outcome.** The
orchestrator/scheduler only ever writes `queued` and `running`; it never reads
your report and never marks a task `done`, `blocked`, or `failed` for you. If you
do not record a terminal status, the task simply returns to `queued` for the next
round. Record status through the CLI — invoke it via the `$HORIZON_BIN` env var
(an absolute path); a bare `horizon` may not be on your shell's PATH.

## The labels

- `queued` — runnable. The scheduler picks up only queued tasks. This is where a
  task rests between rounds when work remains. **Set by the machine (and humans);
  you normally don't.**
- `running` — a session is actively driving it right now. **Set by the machine at
  dispatch.** Don't set this yourself — it means "another session is live," and
  the CLI refuses to start a second run of a `running` task.
- `done` — the assigned objective is **FULLY complete**: the Lean is proved and
  builds, the blueprint node(s) are closed, nothing in the objective remains. Not
  "mostly done", not "the hard part is done", not "a clean commit landed". **Only
  you can set this, and only when it is genuinely, completely finished.** Ground
  verifies it against the diff and the Lean state and will flip a premature `done`
  back — so a false `done` wastes a round, it doesn't save one.
- `blocked` — you cannot make progress: a dependency is missing, a decision is
  needed, or an external constraint stops you. Say why in a comment.
- `failed` — you genuinely could not do the work (not merely "ran out of time" —
  that's just `queued` for next round). Say why in a comment.
- `cancelled` — abandoned by a human. You won't normally set this.

## How to set status

```
"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status done      # objective FULLY complete
"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status blocked   # stuck; explain in a comment
"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status failed    # could not do it; explain
```

Authorship is automatic — the CLI stamps your role (`ground`/`horizon`) from the
run environment; do not pass `--author`. Setting a status appends an auditable
history entry, and if the task has `roadmap_refs` the linked roadmap items are
synced (done→done, blocked/failed→blocked, cancelled→rejected).

## Comment as you work

Leave a short comment whenever you hit a significant step or change the status, so
the ledger tells the story without opening raw logs:

```
"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body "Closed the base case; representability lemma still open."
```

## The one rule to remember

**If the objective is only partly advanced, set nothing.** The task returns to
`queued` and the next round continues it. Reserve `done` for work that is
completely finished — that is the entire point of the status now living with you
instead of being guessed from your report.

text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/Axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon-commit

Commit your work yourself, semantically, as you finish coherent pieces — don't
leave one giant undifferentiated snapshot for the system to sweep up. Good
commits are how the dashboard's change view and a human reviewer understand what
each session actually did.

## How

Use the Horizon CLI (never raw `git` on the ledger — the workspace repo is
out-of-tree with excludes, a secret guard, and provenance trailers that a bare
`git` would bypass):

- `"$HORIZON_BIN" commit -m "<message>" <files…>` — commit the files you changed.
  Paths are relative to your current directory (your project dir) or absolute.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" commit -m "<message>" --changed` — commit everything you
  changed in the project (excludes the shared Horizon state, which the system
  commits separately).

Provenance (run / session / role / task / projects) is stamped automatically —
do **not** pass it. The commit is attributed to your role.

## Messages — math first

Write the message the way you'd tell a mathematician what you did: the result
and the idea, in human-readable prose with LaTeX where it helps; mention Lean
declaration names / files only as supporting detail. Mirror the house style,
e.g. `Prove H^i(X,F)=0 for i>dim X via the Čech-to-derived comparison`. One
coherent step per commit; split unrelated work into separate commits.

## Concurrency — you are not alone

Other runs may be committing to the **same** ledger at the same time. That's
fine and intended (it helps everyone converge faster):

- Commits are a single shared branch — they serialise and never conflict as a
  git *merge*; if `horizon commit` hits contention it already retried, so trust
  its result.
- Commit only the files **you** changed. On a shared worktree your commit can
  still capture another run's in-flight edit to the same file — that's expected
  and acceptable; the message + trailers still record your intent.
- Never `reset`, `rebase`, force-push, or otherwise rewrite the ledger. `horizon
  commit` only ever appends a commit.

## When

Commit at each coherent milestone (a lemma closed, a file completed), not only
at the end. Anything you don't commit is still captured by the system's
end-of-session sweep, but as an unlabelled blob — so commit it yourself to keep

text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/Axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/blueprint-conventions

Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration this node formalizes. Keep it 1-to-1: one
  blueprint node ↔ one Lean declaration, signatures matching.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. If a Lean helper exists with no math counterpart,
  write its LaTeX statement so the 1-to-1 correspondence holds.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One declaration's worth per node.** Don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

data.content: Launching skill: references

text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/Axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/references

`references/` is a **shared library at the workspace root** — one library for
every project — holding the original source material a blueprint is formalised
from (papers, books, notes). It is indexed by `references/manifest.yaml`. Per-
project files live under each project's directory; `references/` does not — it is
always at the workspace root, and `references/**` is writable from any agent.

A blueprint node derived from a source carries a `\source{...}` anchor. Those
anchors are the audit trail from a formal statement back to where it came from,
so they must be **true**, not plausible.

## The one rule: read before you cite

**Never add a `\source{...}` anchor to a source you have not actually read.** Do
not infer a citation from a title, a topic, a theorem number, or your own prior
knowledge of the result. An anchor asserts "this exact statement/proof appears
here" — if you haven't opened the referenced material and confirmed it, you don't
know that, and a wrong anchor is worse than none (it sends the next reader/agent
to the wrong place and launders a guess as provenance).

Concretely, before writing `\source{...}`:
1. Confirm the source exists in `references/manifest.yaml`. If it isn't there,
   get it in first (see below) — don't cite a slug that doesn't resolve.
2. Open the actual content — the TeX, or the transcribed page — and confirm the
   statement/proof you're anchoring is really there.
3. Only then write the anchor.

## Anchor forms — pick by what the source actually is

The manifest's `read` field for each entry tells you which case you're in.

- **The source has LaTeX** (arXiv e-print, an open `.tex`, etc.): read the TeX
  directly and cite the source as a whole — `\source{slug}`. Do **not** invent a
  `page-NNNN`; a TeX source has no rendered pages, so a page number would be
  fabricated. If the manifest documents stable sub-ids for the source (a section
  or label id), you may use `\source{slug:<id>}`, but only an id that exists.
- **The source is PDF-only** (no usable TeX): cite the transcribed page,
  `\source{slug:page-NNNN}`, where `page-NNNN` is a real file under
  `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` that you have read. If that page hasn't
  been transcribed yet, transcribe it first (below) — don't cite a page that
  doesn't exist on disk.

Multiple anchors may be comma-separated: `\source{slug:page-0042, other:page-0007}`.

## Getting a source into the library

Don't fetch and stash sources ad hoc. Spawn the **`reference-retriever`** subagent
(by name, through your engine's native subagent mechanism) with whatever you have
— topic, arXiv ID, DOI, title, URL, target page range. It downloads the original
(preferring TeX, keeping the PDF), verifies the file is real (not a paywall/login
page named `.pdf`), organises it under `references/<slug>/`, and registers it in
`references/manifest.yaml`. Wait for it, then cite from what it wrote.

## Extracting the LaTeX from a PDF-only source

When there is no reliable TeX and you need the actual math (to read it, or to cite
a page), **extract it with the proper tool — don't eyeball the PDF and paraphrase.**
The extraction path is the **`page-transcriber`** subagent, which renders each page
to an image and **vision-transcribes** it into one self-contained
`references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` per page.

- **Vision, never OCR.** OCR mangles math (subscripts, operators, alignment);
  reading the rendered page image with a vision model preserves it. This is a hard
  rule of the transcription flow.
- **A small vision model is usually enough.** Faithful page transcription doesn't
  need a frontier model — a cheap vision-capable model (e.g. Haiku) running in the
  background typically suffices, which is what the config is for:

  ```yaml
  references:
    transcription:
      harness: <optional harness>
      model: <cheap vision-capable model, e.g. a Haiku-class model>
  ```

  Don't pick the model inside the prompt; pin it in config so every transcription
  uses the same cheap vision model. When unset it falls back to the subagent/Ground
  harness.
- **Keep each call ≤5 pages.** Longer ranges lose accuracy; split a big range
  across several `page-transcriber` calls.

## Reading transcriptions correctly

- A transcribed page is `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` where `NNNN` is the
  **PDF page index**, which often differs from the printed page number. The
  manifest entry's `read` field records the `page_offset` and any fallback that
  actually worked — respect it when mapping "Theorem 3.4 on p. 12" to a file.

Mechanism: with `P := (Pic⁰_{X/k})_red`, `A := Pic⁰_{P/k}`, and `B* := Pic⁰_{B/k}`, normalize a universal sheaf on `X × B*` two ways (`ξ`, `β` L3971–3972) to get a bijection `{a : B* → P, a(0)=0} ≅ {b : X → B, b(x)=0}` (via the Comparison theorem B1); then `1_P ↔ u : X → A` and every `b` factors uniquely through `u`. **Costs:** (i) it is stated over an **algebraically closed** field (descent to general `k` needed — cleanest via uniqueness ⇒ Galois-equivariance ⇒ descent of `g`, requiring descent of morphisms A8); (ii) it needs `B ≅ B**` — **double duality**, i.e. `Pic⁰` of an abelian variety being an abelian variety of the same dimension, citing `rmk:Ablsch` L3920 which in turn cites **Mumford AV §13** (`[Mm70, §13]` L3939, `[Mm70, Cor. p.132]` L3955) and Mumford's smoothness argument `[Mm65, pp.117–118]` — full dual-abelian-variety theory, **[RG]**; (iii) it needs **projectivity of abelian varieties over a field** (Milne §6 / Mumford) since Thm 4.8 must apply to `A`; (iv) it produces the Albanese as `Ĵ = Pic⁰(Pic⁰(C))`, so landing on the challenge's `Jacobian C = J` itself additionally needs **autoduality** `A_L^* : Ĵ ≅ J` (`rmk:Jac` L4006–4015, deferred to [EGK, Thm 2.1] — *not proved in Kleiman*). 132	## 5. (c) How base change of the Picard scheme works
133	
134	- **Core fact (`ex:bschg` L2112, `ans:bschg` L5111):** formation of `Pic_{X/S}` commutes with **arbitrary** base change `S' → S`, and the proof is *purely formal*: for `T ∈ Sch/S'`, étale covers of `T` qua `S'`-scheme = étale covers qua `S`-scheme, so `Pic_{(X_{S'}/S')ét}(T) = Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T)`, while `(Pic_{X/S} ×_S S')(T) = Pic_{X/S}(T)`. **No cohomology, no flatness of `S'/S` needed.** Applied with `S = Spec k`, `S' = Spec L`.
135	- **Identity-component step:** `(Pic_{C/k})_L ⊇ (Pic⁰)_L = (Pic_{C_L/L})⁰` needs `lem:agps(3)` L2883–2885: `G⁰` is geometrically connected because it is connected with a `k`-point (EGA IV 4.5.14), so its formation commutes with field extension. This is the **only mathematical content** in `baseChangeIso`.
136	- **Group compatibility:** the composite iso is induced by an isomorphism of group-valued functors, so it upgrades to `Grp (Over (Spec L))` and matches `(baseChange k L).mapGrp` (which exists in mathlib and preserves the Cartesian group structure since `Over.pullback` preserves finite limits) — plumbing, no math.

72	4. **Generic h⁰ computations** (Milne 5.2, 7.1): `h⁰(D+D'−gP) = 1` on a nonempty open of `C^(g)×C^(g)` — needs RR *with* the index term (Riemann inequality alone gives ≥; the `=1` upper bound on an open set needs semicontinuity of `h⁰` in families (Milne quotes I 4.2 = cohomology-and-base-change) plus the `i(D)` decrement lemma 5.2(a), whose Milne proof uses `H¹(L(D))^∨ = Γ(Ω(−D))` — i.e. Serre duality. An adelic substitute exists: `i(D) ≤ i(D−Q) ≤ i(D)+deg Q` monotonicity from the χ-ledger, but the *existence of Q dropping i by exactly deg Q on an open set* is again duality-grade.) Also cohomology-and-base-change for families on `C×T/T`: **ABSENT** from mathlib.

76	8. **Recovering the functor** (Milne 7.6): even after Weil's construction one re-proves `J ≅ P⁰_C` locally via the same `q_*L` machinery as (5) — i.e., the Weil route does **not** avoid the Pic-functor comparison that the challenge's `Jacobian.functor` (pullback of line bundles), `baseChangeIso`, and `exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` need.
77	
78	### 2.2 Frank feasibility verdict
79	
80	**Not viable as the primary route for this challenge; strictly dominated by Pic⁰-style routes.** Reasons: (i) obligations 1–3 and 6 are large from-scratch theories absent from mathlib (quotients by finite groups, relative divisors, cohomology-and-base-change, birational-group globalization) — jointly comparable to or exceeding the FGA route's Quot-scheme debt; (ii) obligation 4 smuggles duality-grade RR back in; (iii) the challenge's deliverables are *functorial* (`functor`, `map_comp`, `baseChangeIso` cocycle, `baseChange_ofCurve`), and Weil's construction produces a bare variety whose functoriality must be re-derived through the Pic functor anyway (Milne 7.6, Rmk 7.7). 85	
86	### (a) Jac := Pic⁰ (fppf/zariski-sheaf or functor-of-points), curve-specific proofs of the instances — RECOMMENDED SPINE
87

So the challenge's smoothness instance reduces to: (i) `Jacobian C` locally of finite type, (ii) geometrically reduced, (iii) `GrpObj` — no deformation theory. What remains for `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` is the **dimension = g** identification, i.e. `T₀J ≅ H¹(C,𝒪_C)` (Milne III 2.1: pure functor-of-points computation on `k[ε]`, `Pic(C_ε) → Pic(C)` kernel `= H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` via `1+aε`) — the old draft's named sorry `finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne` (T16 C-0015, "W12"); its dual-numbers cocycle substrate (`Pic0DualNumberCocycle`) was repaired and sorry-free at freeze.

93	
94	What breaks / remains hard: **properness and geometric irreducibility of Pic⁰, and representability itself** — these are exactly the FGA-lane pillars (other agent's survey). Curve-specific substitutes: properness via the valuative criterion using "line bundles on `C × Spec K` extend over `C × Spec 𝒪_v`" (regular 2-dimensional total space; needs codim-2 line-bundle extension = a Weil-divisor-to-line-bundle roundtrip on a regular surface — **ABSENT** from mathlib, no scheme-level divisor theory at all: verified no `WeilDivisor`/`CartierDivisor`/`Scheme.Pic`, only `CommRing.Pic` in `Mathlib/RingTheory/PicardGroup.lean`); or properness+irreducibility via a surjection from `C^(g)` (pulls in §2 obligations 1–3). 95	
96	### (b) Rigidity lemma for the UP — ALREADY PROVED ONCE, CHEAP TO REBUILD
97	
98	`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/AlgebraicJacobian/RigidityLemma.lean:763` `theorem rigidity_lemma` — **sorry-free** (iter-162; the file's 4 `sorry` strings are all in comments — verified): over `IsAlgClosed k̄`, `X` proper, `X⊗Y` geometrically irreducible + reduced + LFT, `Z` separated: `f(x,y₀) const ⟹ f = snd ≫ g`. Same file derives Milne Cor 1.5 (additive decomposition over a product) and Cor 1.2 (pointed map of AVs is a homomorphism) in `GrpObj` hom-group language. Mathlib: **ABSENT** (no `rigidity` anywhere in `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry` — verified). Sources: Mumford p.43 (PDF p.54) Rigidity Form I; Milne Thm 1.1 (p.8, hypotheses: first factor complete, product geometrically irreducible — the challenge's instance set matches). This is the engine for: uniqueness in `exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`, "factorization is a homomorphism", and `comp_ofCurve`-style normalizations. Verdict: rebuild it (the old draft's decomposition `rigidity_snd_lift` → `rigidity_core` → `rigidity_eqOn_dense_open` → affine-constant bridge is a proven, reusable design); budget small-to-medium.
99

101	
102	Milne 3.13 + 3.14 + 5.6(c): `Div^r_C` is representable by `C^(r)` (for curves — no Hilbert scheme needed if `C^(r)` is built as in §2.1), the Abel map `Div^r → Pic^r` has fibres `ℙ(Γ(C,L(D)))`, and for `r > 2g−2` it is smooth surjective with ℙ^{r−g}-fibres. This is the classical engine for **properness + geometric irreducibility + dimension of Pic⁰ at once** (image of proper irreducible `C^(r)`). Obligations: §2.1 items 1–4 minus the birational group law. It shares with Weil the Sym^r debt but drops obligations 6–8; if the rebuild ever needs properness non-FGA, this is the least-bad geometric route. What breaks: cohomology-and-base-change (I 4.2) for `q_*L` on `C×T/T` remains unavoidable (**ABSENT** in mathlib; old draft's B3/02KG work — T16 C-0015 — was a partial substitute: `Stacks 02KG i=0 for affine f along arbitrary non-flat g` DISCHARGED).

If J is defined via Pic⁰-representability (however obtained), Milne 5.1(a) (birational `f^(g)`) + 6.7 give dimension-g, irreducibility (dominated by irreducible `C^(g)`), and properness (surjective image of proper). Still needs Sym^g (obligation §2.1.1–2) and generic `h⁰=1` (§2.1.4).
105	
106	### (e) χ-ledger–first RR (skip duality where possible). The old draft's Tier-2 ledger over `K(C)` (`ChiLedger.lean`, 0 sorries at freeze for: `sectionOfDivisor`(+Submodule forms), `coboundary`, `H1`/`H1Twist`/`windowMap`, `windowMap_injective`, `linearSystem_inf_overlap_eq`, `localStepQuot_injective`, `localStep_finrank_le_residueDeg`, `residueDeg`, `chi_le_ell`, `riemann_inequality` (conditional form)) plus T16 C-0015's "P2-kit GREEN: chi(O_C)=1−genus anchored + h0/h1/chi carrier (37 decls)". **Unproved at freeze** (blueprint `\notready`/no-`\leanok`): the Mittag-Leffler surjectivity half of the twist sequence (`thm:adelic_twist_exact_sequence` — needs weak approximation on the affine chart), `thm:adelic_dim_adele_quotient_eq_degree` (local dimension count = residue degree, gated on `IsConstantField`, whose instance `GateInstances.lean` discharged), the telescoped `thm:adelic_chi_eq_chi_zero_add_degree`, and all of Tier 3 (`HasResiduePairing`, `HasSerreDuality` gates — **no Lean file was ever created**; blueprint cites `Adelic/Duality.lean` in `archon:covers` but the file is ABSENT from `RiemannRoch/Adelic/`). Verdict: the ledger through `χ(D) = deg D + 1 − g` and the Riemann inequality is 1–2 nodes from closed and duality-free; **Serre duality/i(D)-vanishing (`deg D > 2g−2 ⟹ i(D)=0`) is the single deepest unbuilt stone** of the adelic lane, needed by anything that wants sharp `h⁰` (Weil/CaCl routes §2, §3(c)(d), and Castelnuovo-style boundedness in Quot endgames). If needed, build it function-field-theoretically from Papaioannou Thm 1.23/1.25/1.26 + Vater Ch. 1 local components (statements in §1.4) — not scheme-theoretic duality (mathlib has **no** Serre duality, dualizing sheaf, trace map, or coherent proper-pushforward cohomology; re-verified against the current checkout, and `analogies/serre-duality.md` estimated 3,000–8,000 LOC for a scheme-level build).
107	
108	### (f) Genus-0 note: `genus C = 0 ⟹ C ≅ ℙ¹` (needed if any route case-splits on g=0; challenge itself doesn't force it). `analogies/rrbridge-survey.md` (iter-168) verdict: every Hartshorne IV.1.3.5 ingredient ABSENT from mathlib; no shortcut. Function-field alternative now in-library: CFF Prop 14.6 (`g=0` + degree-1 place ⟹ `L=K(s)` rational) — still needs the "curve determined by its function field" bridge (ABSENT; `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Normalization.lean` and `SpreadingOut.lean` exist as partial substrate).
109	
110	---
111	
112	## 4. UNIVERSAL PROPERTY (Albanese) — exact statements and the extension chain
113	
114	### 4.1 What the references actually prove
115	
116	- **Milne III Prop 6.1** (p. 104 / PDF p.110; standing hypotheses of Ch. III §6: `C` complete nonsingular of genus `g > 0` over `k` with `P ∈ C(k)`, `J = Jac C` exists): for any map `φ : C → A` into an abelian variety with `φ(P) = 0` there is a **unique homomorphism** `ψ : J → A` with `φ = ψ ∘ f_P`. Proof chain (verbatim structure): (1) `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ Σφ(Pᵢ) : C^g → A` is symmetric ⟹ factors through `C^(g)` [needs Sym UP]; (2) this defines a *rational map* `J ⇢ A` via the birational `f^(g) : C^(g) → J` [Milne 5.1(a), which itself needs generic `h⁰=1` = 5.2(b)]; (3) **Milne I Thm 3.2** makes it a regular map [see 4.2]; (4) it is a homomorphism by **I Cor 1.2** [rigidity]; (5) uniqueness because `J = W_g = f_P(C)+⋯+f_P(C)` [image-sum density]. 
117	- **Milne III Prop 6.4 + Rmk 6.5** (p. 105): the two-variable form `φ : C×C → A`, `φ(Δ)=0` factors uniquely through `F(P₁,P₂) = f_P(P₁) − f_P(P₂)`; `F` is defined over `k` without a rational point (Galois-descent paragraph before 6.4, using uniqueness); this is "the Albanese variety of C in the sense of Lang 1959". Note the descent pattern of 6.4's proof (uniqueness ⟹ Galois-equivariance ⟹ defined over k) is exactly the tool for the challenge's non-algebraically-closed base and interacts well with `baseChangeIso`.
118	- **Milne I Thm 1.1 (rigidity)**, Cor 1.2 (map of AVs = homomorphism ∘ translation), Cor 1.4 (commutativity), Cor 1.5 (product decomposition) — pp. 8–9; hypotheses as in §3(b).
119	- **Mumford** provides the same rigidity primitive (Form I, p.43) and Corollaries 1–3 (incl. `Hom(S,X)×Hom(T,X) ≅ Hom(S×T,X)` for complete pointed varieties, p.44); per `references/mumford-abelian-varieties.md` there is **no packaged "Mor(ℙ¹,A) constant"** in Mumford §4 — that is Milne Prop 3.10 (p.20, PDF p.26: unirational source ⟹ constant). The theorem-of-the-cube (Mumford §6 p.55; Milne §5) is **not needed** for the Albanese UP chain above — it enters only for autoduality/polarization (Milne 6.6) and projectivity, which the challenge does not ask for.
120	
121	### 4.2 The codimension-1 extension theorem chain (exact)
122	
123	`Milne I Thm 3.1` (p.15, PDF p.22; **proof read in full**): a rational map `V ⇢ W`, `V` normal, `W` complete, is defined off a closed set of codim ≥ 2. Curve case: graph closure + "complete nonsingular curve determined by function field"; general case: valuative criterion of properness at the DVR of a prime divisor of the complement.
124	`Milne I Lemma 3.3` (p.16–17, PDF p.23–24): into a group variety `G`, the undefined locus is empty or **pure codim 1** — via `Φ(x,y) = φ(x)φ(y)⁻¹`, "`φ` defined at x ⟺ `Φ` defined at (x,x) ⟺ `Im(𝒪_{G,e}) ⊆ 𝒪_{V×V,(x,x)}`", then pole-divisor purity of `div(f)_∞ ∩ Δ` (Krull height 1).
125	`Milne I Thm 3.2` = 3.1 + 3.3: rational map from a **nonsingular** variety to an **abelian** (complete group) variety is a morphism.
126	Old-draft state of this chain (from `informal/milne-lemma-3.3.md`, read in full; lives in `Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean`, `Albanese/DifferenceMap.lean`, `Albanese/PolePurity.lean`): Milne 3.1-analogue (`indeterminacy_codimGe2_of_smooth_of_complete`) **proved**; difference map + domain lower bound + the algebraic content of the hard direction of "Φ defined at (x,x) ⟹ φ defined at x" **proved**; pole purity 4a (`exists_specializes_coheight_eq_one_of_notMem_stalk_range`) **proved**; remaining genuine gaps at freeze: (i) topological existence of the auxiliary point `u` (uses geometric irreducibility of the fibre — this is *why* the challenge carries `GeometricallyIrreducible`), (ii) descent of definedness along `pr₁` (flagged as an fppf-descent build), (iii) sub-step 3 (germ pullback at `e`, with the non-dominance caveat: replace `G` by the closure of the image, a subgroup), (iv) 4b (pole divisor restricted to the diagonal, needs Hauptidealsatz on `X×X`). The note also records the standing warning: do **not** use `extend_of_codimOneFree` (false: `ℙ²⇢ℙ¹`). Mathlib substrate for all of this: `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Birational/RationalMap.lean` is rich (verified: `PartialMap`, `RationalMap`, `domain`, `dense_domain`, `fromFunctionField`, `equivFunctionField(Over)`, `compHom`, separated-target equivalence lemmas) — **but has no extension/indeterminacy-codimension theorems** (verified by scanning all decls).
127	
128	### 4.3 Fit to the challenge statement (`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`)
129	
130	The challenge quantifies over **arbitrary** `A : Over (Spec k)` with `[Smooth A.hom] [IsProper A.hom] [GrpObj A] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]` — not "abelian varieties". Bridging facts, now free or cheap: commutativity = `isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral` (needs geometrically *integral*: reduced comes from smooth — same §1.3 wrinkle); such an `A` is exactly Milne's abelian variety after base change to `k̄`. Milne's UP proof needs, over `k̄`: Sym^g UP + birational `f^(g)` (§2 debt) + Thm 3.2 chain (§4.2) + rigidity (§3(b), proved once already); then descend uniqueness-first to `k` (Milne 6.4-pattern). **No reference in the library proves the Albanese UP without the symmetric-power + rational-map-extension machinery**; the alternative (divisorial-correspondence UP, Milne 1.7/Thm 1.6 ⟹ Exercise 1.9) is the Pic-representability route — i.e., the UP either goes through §2-style geometry or through the universal line bundle (FGA lane). A rebuild wanting the *shortest* honest UP should state it via the universal divisorial correspondence `M_P` (Milne 1.7): the factorization `g : Jacobian C ⟶ A` is produced by classifying `(1×φ)^*(pullback of a normalized Poincaré-type sheaf on C×A)`… but that requires `A`'s own Pic — circular for arbitrary `A`. Hence: **rigidity + extension chain is the only known non-FGA UP proof**, and its Lean-hardest stones are the four §4.2 gaps.
131	
132	---
133	
134	## 5. Mathlib v4.31.0 inventory relevant to alternative routes (all verified this session)
135	
136	PRESENT: `IsProper` (`Morphisms/Proper.lean:42`), `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` (+ base-change stability, `Morphisms/Smooth.lean:135,166`), `GeometricallyIrreducible/-Reduced/-Integral/-Connected` (`Geometrically/`), `GrpObj`/`Grp C`/`mapGrp*` (`CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Grp.lean`, `Cartesian/Grp.lean` incl. `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`, `commutator`, `conj`), **abelian-variety facts** (`Group/Abelian.lean`, `Group/Smooth.lean`), ZMT + `IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite` (`ZariskisMainTheorem.lean`), valuative criterion (`ValuativeCriterion.lean`), `Proj` + properness (`ProjectiveSpectrum/Proper.lean`) + `Proj.fromOfGlobalSections` (`ProjectiveSpectrum/Basic.lean:439`), rational maps (`Birational/RationalMap.lean`), normalization (`Normalization.lean`), function fields (`FunctionField.lean` incl. `functionField_isFractionRing_of_isAffineOpen`), Dedekind/valuation stack (`RingTheory/DedekindDomain/{Ideal,AdicValuation,FiniteAdeleRing}.lean`: `HeightOneSpectrum`, `valuation`, `FiniteAdeleRing`), `ClassGroup` (`RingTheory/ClassGroup/`), sheaf cohomology `Sheaf.H` + Čech complex functor + MV LES (`CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/{Basic,Cech,MayerVietoris}.lean`), Grothendieck-abelian ⟹ `HasExt` (`CategoryTheory/Abelian/GrothendieckCategory/`), ring invariants `A^G` (`RingTheory/Invariant/`).

138	ABSENT (all grep-verified): Riemann–Roch (any form), Serre duality / dualizing sheaf / trace morphism, scheme-level Weil/Cartier divisors, `Scheme.Pic`, degree of line bundles, symmetric powers of schemes, quotients of schemes by finite groups, relative effective Cartier divisors / `Div^r` functor, cohomology-and-base-change, rigidity lemma, Albanese anything, rational-map extension/indeterminacy theorems, smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced, Weil differentials/residues, `ProjectiveSpace` as such (only `Proj 𝒜` + `AffineSpace`).
139

141	
142	- Genus lane architecture (§1.2–1.3): `RiemannRoch/Adelic/{Substrate,Cokernel,P1BaseCase,P1ChartData,NonconstantToP1,FiniteMapToP1,FinitenessP1,GenusFiniteness,CechComparisonGate,GenusUnconditional}.lean` + `RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor.lean` (`PrimeDivisor`, `WeilDivisor := PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ`, `RationalMap.order`, `IsRegularInCodimensionOne`) — endorse wholesale as the rebuild's genus route; the MV-slice trick made the lane *gate-free*.

# Route decision — the mathematical architecture of the rebuild

*2026-07-11, Fable-5 design session. Inputs: a 5-agent survey (mathlib v4.31.0 capability
inventory; old-draft map; Kleiman/FGA route DAG; alternative-routes survey; operational
lessons). Survey reports are archived in the session scratchpad; their load-bearing
conclusions are restated here so this document is self-contained.*

This document fixes the route for all 14 protected targets in
`AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` and the design rules every wave must follow.
It is the map; the blueprint is the mathematics; the Lean tree is the proof.

## 1. The route in one paragraph

**`Jacobian C := Pic⁰_{C/k}`**, the identity component of the scheme representing the
étale-sheafified relative Picard functor of `C/k` (Kleiman, *The Picard Scheme*, FGA
Explained ch. 5). Representability is the central mountain (Grothendieck's Thm 4.8,
specialized hard to a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over a field).
The Albanese universal property is proved Milne-style (*Abelian Varieties* III.6.1):
symmetric powers `C^(g) → J` birational, rational maps into abelian varieties extend
(Milne I.3.2 = I.3.1 + Lemma 3.3), rigidity makes the factorization a homomorphism,
uniqueness descends from `k̄` to `k`. The genus is `g(C) := dim_k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` with
`H¹` the derived-functor cohomology of the Zariski site of `C` valued in `ModuleCat k`,
computed by a pinned 2-affine-cover Mayer–Vietoris cokernel and proved finite by the
two-lattice ladder over a finite map `C → ℙ¹`. Every functorial target (`functor`,
`baseChangeIso`, the coherences) is a uniqueness-of-representing-object corollary of a
single pinned `RepresentableBy` datum — never a `Classical.choice` extraction.

Why not the alternatives (survey verdicts):

- **Weil group-chunk construction (Sym^g + birational group law): rejected.** Its
  obligations (scheme quotients by finite groups, relative divisors,
  cohomology-and-base-change, Weil's globalization theorem, plus a descent problem for
  pointless curves — the challenge's `Jacobian` takes **no rational point**) meet or
  exceed the FGA debt, and the functorial targets would still have to be re-derived
  through the Pic functor afterwards (Milne III.7.6). FGA's Thm 4.8 needs no point;
  that is a structural advantage for this exact statement file.
- **Kleiman's own Albanese derivation (`rmk:Alb`): rejected** — it outsources dual
  abelian varieties, autoduality (`Ĵ ≅ J`, [EGK Thm 2.1], unproved in our references)
  and projectivity of abelian varieties. Milne III.6.1 is strictly lighter and its
  ingredients (Sym^g, Riemann–Roch) are shared with the `Div^d`-representability leg,
  so their cost is amortized.

## 2. Ground truth about mathlib v4.31.0 (verified in the checkout, not from memory)

**Gifts to design around** (all present):

- Group objects: `GrpObj`, bundled `Grp C`, `Functor.mapGrp/mapGrpIdIso/mapGrpCompIso/
  mapGrpNatIso` — the challenge's vocabulary, complete. **`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`**:
  a representing object of a group-valued functor gets `GrpObj` for free.
- `AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Abelian.lean`: `isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`
  (proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field is commutative) — the
  rigidity *corollary* is already a theorem.
- `AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Smooth.lean`: `smooth_of_grpObj` (geometrically reduced +
  locally finite type group scheme over a field ⇒ smooth) — kills the deformation-theory
  half of smoothness; what remains of `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` is
  `T₀J ≅ H¹(C,𝒪_C)` plus dimension bookkeeping.
- `Sites/Representability.lean` (Zariski sheaf glued from representable opens is
  representable, Stacks 01JJ), `subcanonical_zariskiTopology`, the étale/fppf/fpqc sites.
- `ZariskisMainTheorem.lean`: `IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the
  finite-map-to-ℙ¹ leg shrinks.
- Sheaf cohomology `Sheaf.H` via `Ext` + Grothendieck-abelian `HasExt`/`EnoughInjectives`
  + the Mayer–Vietoris LES (`Sites/SheafCohomology/`) — at `AddCommGrpCat`; the
  `ModuleCat k` twin is ours to build (de-risked: the old draft did it).
- `IsProper`/`SmoothOfRelativeDimension`/`Geometrically*` with exactly the stability
  instances the frozen file consumes; valuative criterion over arbitrary valuation rings;
  `Proj` + its properness; function fields; Dedekind/`HeightOneSpectrum` valuation stack;
  `RingTheory/Invariant` (`A^G`); rational maps (`Birational/RationalMap.lean` — no
  extension theorems though).

**Load-bearing absences** (each is ours to build; nothing above Layer A of the DAG exists):
coherent cohomology of schemes (any `H^i(X,F)`, `R^i f_*`, base change, finiteness,
vanishing); line bundles / `Pic` of a scheme; Weil/Cartier divisors, degrees, `L(D)`;
Riemann–Roch / Serre duality in any form; ampleness / projectivity vocabulary / `𝒪(d)` /
Serre finiteness; Hilbert/Quot/Grassmannian schemes; quotients of schemes (finite groups
or equivalence relations); symmetric powers; relative effective divisors; rigidity;
rational-map extension theorems; smooth ⇒ geometrically reduced; Auslander–Buchsbaum;
DVR refinement of the valuative criterion; genus (zero hits in all of Mathlib).

## 3. Definitions of record (the semantic pins)

- **genus**: `genus C := Module.finrank k (H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C))` where `Hⁿₖ(C, F)` is the
  Ext-based cohomology of the (essentially small) Zariski site of `C` with values in
  `ModuleCat k`, applied to the structure sheaf viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules.
  *Not* a Čech-carrier definition: the derived definition is canonical
  (cover-independent by construction), mathlib-idiomatic, and the MV (0,1)-slice
  gives the 2-cover cokernel computation as a theorem, gate-free (old draft proved
  this bridge end to end; we re-derive it).
- **Jacobian**: the representing object of the degree-0 part of the étale-sheafified
  relative Picard functor, carried as a **pinned `RepresentableBy` datum** (data, not
  `Nonempty`), from which `instGrpObj` is `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`, `functor.map` is
  precomposition of represented functors, and `baseChangeIso` + coherences are
  uniqueness-of-representing-object arguments.
- **ofCurve**: the Abel–Jacobi map `t ↦ [𝒪(Γ_t − P_T)]` via graph divisors
  (`Div¹_{C/k} = C`), landing in `Pic⁰` because `C` is connected and `P ↦ 0`.
- **Albanese UP**: Milne III.6.1 over `k̄`, descended to `k` uniqueness-first
  (Milne 6.4-pattern). Note the challenge asks uniqueness among **plain** `Over`-morphisms;
  rigidity converts any competitor into a homomorphism (it is pointed:
  `η ≫ g = P ≫ ofCurve P ≫ g = P ≫ f = η`), and homomorphisms agreeing on the
  generating curve agree.

## 4. Proof-obligation DAG (cost-ordered waves)

Difficulty: [R] routine, [S] substantial, [RG] research-grade-for-mathlib.
The four [RG] clusters are: representability (B4), Albanese (N12), properness (N5),
and the coherent-cohomology substrate they stand on. Everything else is [R]/[S] given
its predecessors.

### Wave 1 — curve substrate + the genus lane (fully de-risked; do first)
1. `Curve/Basic` [R–S]: standing consequences of the hypothesis bundle — integral,
   quasi-compact, separated; `Γ(C,𝒪_C) ≅ k` (via mathlib's
   `isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right` + properness `isField`
   facts); function field; stalk dimension ≤ 1 on standard-smooth rel-dim-1 charts.
2. `Curve/GeometricallyReduced` [S]: **smooth ⇒ geometrically reduced** (fibers of a
   smooth morphism are geometrically regular). Mathlib gap under EVERY target: the
   frozen file says `GeometricallyIrreducible`; all the real mathematics needs
   `GeometricallyIntegral`. Settled here once, as an instance.
3. `Cohomology/*` [S]: `ModuleCat k`-valued sheaf cohomology `Hⁿₖ` (Grothendieck-abelian
   ⇒ `HasExt`, universe discipline fixed once); degree-1 vanishing on affines;
   2-affine-cover MV square + `H1Cok` cokernel carrier; the MV (0,1)-slice bridge
   `H¹ₖ(C,𝒪) ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok`.
4. `Curve/MapToP1` [S]: a nonconstant rational function spreads out to a finite
   `π : C → ℙ¹` (ZMT does the heavy lifting now).
5. `Cohomology/Finiteness` + `Genus` [S]: two-lattice ladder ⇒ `Module.Finite k H¹ₖ`;
   **define `genus`, discharge the first protected sorry.**

### Wave 2 — abelian-variety generalities (parallel to late W1)
6. `AbelianVariety/Rigidity` [S]: Mumford Form-I rigidity over `k̄`; Milne I Cor 1.2
   (pointed map of AVs is a homomorphism), Cor 1.5. (Old draft proved this 908-line
   design; re-derive compactly, checking what `Group/Abelian.lean` already covers.)
7. χ-ledger / RR-lite [S]: `h⁰/h¹/χ` for line-bundle-twisted sheaves on `C` via the
   2-cover carrier; `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g`; degree via `deg L := χ(L) − χ(𝒪)`; Riemann
   inequality; principal divisors have degree 0. Feeds N2 (projectivity), Div^d, and
   the Albanese birationality. Serre duality is deferred until a consumer forces it
   (function-field route via Weil differentials if ever needed — never scheme-theoretic).

### Wave 3 — the Picard functor and the gated spine
8. `Picard/LineBundles` [S]: invertible 𝒪-modules on `C ×ₖ T` *modeled by transition
   data on the pinned 2-cover after affine-local refinement of `T`* — no monoidal
   structure on sheaf categories, ever (the old draft burned ~10k lines there; its own
   post-mortem endorses the cocycle model).
9. `Picard/Functor` [S]: the rigidified/étale-sheafified `Pic_{C/k}` on affine test
   schemes; group-valued; degree map; `Pic⁰` sub-functor.
10. `Picard/Witness` [R]: the **`JacobianData C` structure** — representing object +
    pinned `RepresentableBy` + the instance package. Downstream waves consume
    `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable. NEVER a sorried instance
    (typed-sorry data poisons every consumer with `sorryAx`); NEVER `Nonempty` + choice
    (destroys the naturality data that `functor`/`baseChangeIso` need).

### Wave 4 — representability [RG mountain #1]
11. Rigid pushforward engine (Mumford AV II.5 two-term projective replacement;
    `h¹`-vanishing ⇒ `q_*L` locally free of rank χ commuting with base change).
12. Uniform `h¹`-vanishing for large degree; `Div^d` for curves; Grassmannian/ℙ-bundle
    embedding; Σ-opens, equalizer, gluing over `k^s` (Stacks 01JJ); Galois descent to `k`
    (Speiser semilinear descent — landed cleanly in the old draft, re-derive).
    The old draft's judged D3 campaign decomposition (~15–20 milestones) is the map;
    Quot schemes / flattening / Altman–Kleiman are **off-route** (their only Kleiman
    consumer, `lm:qt`, is bypassed by the curve-specific `Div^d` geometry).

### Wave 5 — the abelian-variety package for `Pic⁰` [RG mountains #2, #3]
13. Tangent space `T₀Pic = H¹(C,𝒪)` (dual numbers, truncated exponential) [S];
    smoothness via geometric reducedness at 0 + `smooth_of_grpObj` [S];
    `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C)` assembly [S].
14. Properness [RG]: valuative criterion; extend a line bundle on `C_K` over `C_A`
    (`C_A` regular 2-dimensional ⇒ locally factorial — needs an Auslander–Buchsbaum-grade
    brick; budget explicitly, consider the `C^(g)`-surjection alternative if Sym^g lands
    first for Albanese).
15. Geometric irreducibility: identity-component theory (`lem:agps(3)`: `G⁰` open-closed,
    finite type, geometrically irreducible, formation commutes with field extension) [S].
    This single lemma also powers `baseChangeIso`.

### Wave 6 — Albanese [RG mountain #2]
16. Sym^r C as a scheme (finite-group quotient via Γ-stable affine covers — the old
    draft's Galois-quotient engine design, re-derived) [S–RG]; smoothness of `C^(g)` [S];
    `Div^r ≅ C^(r)` [S] (shared with Wave 4!).
17. Rational-map extension chain: Milne I.3.1 [S], Lemma 3.3 (the four audited substeps;
    two were proved in the old draft) [RG], Thm 3.2 [R given both].
18. Milne III.6.1 assembly over `k̄` [S]; uniqueness-first Galois descent to `k` [S];
    `ofCurve`, `comp_ofCurve`, `exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` discharge.

### Wave 7 — the functorial layer (cheap **by design** if Wave 3's pin is respected)
19. `functor` (pullback of line bundles = precomposition on represented functors;
    laws by uniqueness) [S-tedious]; 20. `baseChangeIso` (étale-site base-change formal
    identity + `(Pic⁰)_L = (Pic_L)⁰` from #15) [S]; 21. coherences + `baseChange_ofCurve`
    (uniqueness of isos intertwining pinned universal elements) [R–S given the pin].

## 5. Design rules (binding for every wave; distilled from the campaign post-mortems)

1. **Keystone funnel.** Every wave funnels to one keystone with a wide parallel base;
   state the *narrowest* form a consumer needs (degree-1-only vanishing beat the full
   Čech-to-derived comparison; i=0 affine base-change bricks beat the `R^i f_*` engine).
2. **Statement audit before proof.** Every pinned statement gets a semantic audit against
   the source before anyone proves it (the old campaign shipped three false-as-pinned
   statements; each cost runs). Counterexamples for rejected pins go in the blueprint.
3. **No sorried data, no choice-extracted witnesses.** Deep pillars are gated as Prop
   classes or explicit structure hypotheses; `sorry` never inhabits a def/instance.
4. **One pinned universal element.** `Jacobian`, `functor`, `baseChangeIso` are all
   defined through the same `RepresentableBy` datum; coherences become uniqueness.
5. **No monoidal sheaf categories; no global adele space; no general `R^i f_*` engine;
   no Quot schemes.** Each is a measured multi-week detour whose consumers have
   cheaper curve-specific substitutes.
6. **Files ≤ 500 lines; mathlib naming; blueprint chapter per Lean directory,
   1-to-1 nodes, `\leanok` only after kernel check; `\source{}` only after reading.**
7. **Verification bar**: `lake build <Module>` (kernel), then `lean_verify` axiom audit
   (`propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound` only). LSP is advisory; `lake env lean`
   is a false oracle (lakefile sets `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`).
8. **Uniform genus.** No genus-0 fork anywhere; `J = Pic⁰` uniformly (the old draft
   deleted a weeks-long genus-0 lane).
9. **Known Lean walls + fixes** (from the ops mining, use as first resort):
   `Over.pullback` instance-opacity → point-level `congrArg` calc chains; defeq-blocked
   `𝟙` → `erw [Category.comp_id]`; functor laws by `subst`-shaped proofs; scoped
   `maxHeartbeats` bumps ≤ 1M (never stack past it — restructure); repeated `binop%`
   products hoisted into a named def; `GrpObj` is data → `letI`; `open scoped MonObj`.

## 6. What "done" means, phase by phase

- **Phase 1**: all 14 protected declarations sorry-free; `lake build` green;
  `#print axioms` on each = standard three; blueprint every node `\leanok` with sources.
- **Phase 2** (only after green): REVIEW.md anchors for the three headline theorems,
  code↔paper correspondence tightening, `ForMathlib/` extraction of the general bricks
  (smooth⇒geometrically reduced, identity-component theory, rigidity, MV `ModuleCat k`
  slice, finite-group quotients, Speiser descent are the obvious PR candidates).

variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-- **Existence of a finite map to the projective line**: on the smooth, proper,
geometrically irreducible curve `C/k` there is a finite `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`.

This is the keystone the two-lattice finiteness argument for `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` consumes.

Intended proof route (see `informal/route-decision.md`, Wave 1 item 4):
1. produce a rational function on `C` transcendental over `k` (an affine chart of the
   relative-dimension-1 smooth curve has a section ring of Krull dimension 1, which cannot be
   algebraic over `k`); this consumes `GeometricallyReduced C.hom`/integrality of `C`, which
   another Wave-1 lane derives from smoothness;
2. extend the rational function to a morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k` using that the local
   rings of `C` at codimension-one points are valuation rings (DVRs): at each point either
   `f` or `1/f` is regular, giving maps to the two charts of `P1 k` which glue;
3. `π` is nonconstant, hence (fibers are proper closed subschemes of the curve not equal to
   it) has finite fibers, hence is locally quasi-finite;
4. conclude with `exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` (Zariski's main theorem).

Only steps 1–3 remain. -/
theorem exists_isFinite_toP1 :
    ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, IsFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom := by
  sorry

/-! ### Preimage bookkeeping for a finite morphism to the projective line

The next wave feeds these to the two-lattice/Mayer–Vietoris finiteness argument: the
preimages of the two standard charts form an affine cover of `C`, with section rings
module-finite over `k[t]`. Everything here only needs `π` finite (indeed mostly just
affine), not how it was constructed. -/

section Preimages

variable {Y : Scheme.{u}} (π : Y ⟶ P1 k)

/-- The preimage of each standard chart of `ℙ¹` under an affine (e.g. finite) morphism is an
affine open. -/
theorem isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen [IsAffineHom π] (i : Fin 2) :
    IsAffineOpen (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k i) :=
  (P1.isAffineOpen_chartOpen k i).preimage π

/-- The preimages of the two standard charts of `ℙ¹` cover the source. -/
theorem preimage_chartOpen_sup :
    π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊔ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1 = ⊤ := by
  refine le_antisymm le_top fun x _ => ?_
  have h : π.base x ∈ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊔ P1.chartOpen k 1 := by
    rw [P1.chartOpen_sup]
    trivial
  rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup] at h ⊢
  exact h

/-- For a finite morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, the section ring of the preimage of a standard chart
is module-finite over the section ring of the chart (that is, over `k[t]`, via
`P1.chartSectionsEquiv₀`/`₁`). -/
theorem finite_app_chartOpen [IsFinite π] (i : Fin 2) :
    RingHom.Finite (π.app (P1.chartOpen k i)).hom :=
  π.finite_app _ (P1.isAffineOpen_chartOpen k i)

/-- For a finite morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, the section ring of the preimage of the chart
overlap is module-finite over the section ring of the overlap (that is, over the Laurent
polynomial ring, via `P1.overlapSectionsEquiv`). -/
theorem finite_app_overlap [IsFinite π] :
    RingHom.Finite (π.app (Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)
      (X 0 * X 1))).hom :=
  π.finite_app _ (P1.isAffineOpen_overlap k)

end Preimages

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-- The genus of a smooth proper curve: the `k`-dimension of the first cohomology group
`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski
site of `C` (`Scheme.moduleKSheaf`), with cohomology the `Ext` from the constant sheaf

  Module.finrank k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)
